newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Put buyers see test of Bund support.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Put buyers see test of Bund support.

text.p: Put buyers sprang into action in the Bund options pit at LIFFE on Tuesday, plumping up implied volatility on the put side, traders said. Implied volatility of call options held firm.

Traders said there was no negative news to prompt investors to expect a drop in the futures, but the lack of positive news might force a test of recent support. "The market is trying to break 101.00 to go further down," Mourad Amellel, trader at Transoptions Finance in London. "People are thinking the market is too expensive and needs a correction and we are not waiting for any good news."
He said August par puts were the most active strike with a continental European and a Japanese bank buying in bulk. LIFFE data showed 8,144 lots at the 100.00 strike had changed hands by 1035 GMT.
A broker at GNI in London said put spread buyers were also active at the 100.00-99.00 strike.
"Paper loves the par puts," he said, referring to institutions rather than locals.
Implied volatility of the August 101.00 straddle was quoted at around 5.3 percent middle, little changed from Monday, though puts were slightly bid.
The sale of the par puts went through at volatility of around 5.7/5.8 percent, traders said.
On the call side, the August 102.00 strike was the most active with 2,335 lots changing hands.
September Bund futures were quoted at 101.29, up one basis point from Monday's settlement.
Amellel said investors expected the market to test support around 101.00, the base at the beginning of June for the September Bunds' latest spurt higher.
He said news that Germany would issue a 30-year bond for up to 10 billion marks early next week may put pressure on prices.

Earlier, the west German state of Bavaria reported the cost of living rose 0.2 percent in June from May and 1.6 percent from June 1996. Baden-Wuerttemberg reported consumer prices climbed 0.2 percent in the month and 1.4 percent year-on-year.
The data were slightly worse than the market expected. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
